quarterly_data.quarter: AstraZeneca press release: Update on SERENA-4 Phase III trial of Etcamah in (09-11-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: AstraZeneca announced (as inside information) that the SERENA-4 Phase III trial of Etcamah (camizestrant) plus palbociclib versus anastrozole plus palbociclib did not meet its primary endpoint of progression-free survival in upfront 1st-line ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, although a numerical improvement was observed. The trial enrolled 1,371 patients with no prior systemic treatment for advanced disease; safety was consistent with each medicine's known profile and data will be shared in due course. Susan Galbraith (EVP, Oncology Haematology R&D) said the company is 'disappointed by the SERENA-4 outcome', that it 'reinforces the importance of ESR1 testing for patients on first-line therapy', and that the company remains confident in Etcamah's long-term potential in early breast cancer, where the CAMBRIA-1 and CAMBRIA-2 Phase III adjuvant trials encompass approximately 10,000 patients. Etcamah remains approved in the US, EU, Japan and several other countries in the ESR1-mutation setting based on SERENA-6.
quarterly_data.figure: SERENA-4 PFS primary endpoint not met (numerical improvement only); 1,371 patients; CAMBRIA-1 and CAMBRIA-2 approximately 10,000 patients
